metadata.title: Trump says he must be involved in selecting Iran's next leader

left: U.S. President Donald Trump stated he must be involved in selecting Iran's next supreme leader and rejected Mojtaba Khamenei, calling him a 'lightweight'.
Iran launched retaliatory attacks against Israel, U.S. bases, and neighboring countries amid escalating conflict.
Israel issued evacuation warnings for Beirut's southern suburbs amid intensified fighting involving Hezbollah and U.N. peacekeepers.
Iran condemned the sinking of its warship by the U.S. Navy as an 'atrocity at sea,' prompting calls for violence against Israel and Trump by Iranian clerics.
center: On Thursday, President Donald Trump told Axios he plans to play a direct role in choosing Iran's next supreme leader during an eight-minute phone interview.
Speaking amid a joint U.S.-Israel bombing campaign, the news arrived on the fifth day after strikes linked to the death of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
The president dismissed Mojtaba Khamenei as unacceptable and called him a lightweight, comparing U.S. influence to his involvement with Delcy Rodríguez in Venezuela.
With no official successor announced, Iran has not yet named a new Supreme Leader, and Trump said he would reject any successor continuing the late leader's policies.
The push to reshape Iran's leadership ties to stated U.S.-Israeli goals to topple the government, while rising oil prices this week surged over $10 per barrel, deepening global oil markets' impact.
right: US President Donald Trump stated he must be involved in selecting Iran's next Supreme Leader after the killing of Ali Khamenei in a US-Israel airstrike.
Trump called Mojtaba Khamenei, the late leader's son and possible successor, a "lightweight," and rejected his succession.
Trump compared his desired role in Iran's leadership selection to his involvement in Venezuela's leadership change involving Delcy Rodriguez.
Trump warned that a leader continuing Ali Khamenei's policies could lead to future conflict with the US.
